story.value: Uranium is named after the planet Uranus.
The German chemist Martin-Heinrich Klaproth discovered uranium in 1789.
Uranium metal was first isolated by the French chemist Eugène-Melchior Peligot in 1841.

uses.value: Uranium is most commonly used in the nuclear power industry to generate electricity.
Uranium is used as a shield against radiation.
Uranium metal is used as a target to produce high-energy X-rays.
Uranium compounds have been used for centuries to color glass.
